answer: Timber billing with lantern snapshots: every action spends one timber credit minted only by a 30-second compute proof, non-transferable, capped at 30 per account. Each epoch a lantern node freezes balance and spend into a public snapshot; the river of state must show steady consumption, and sudden inflow fails cross-snapshot checks. A farm's k puppets each mint credits at the same per-unit cost with no bulk discount, and each must keep a clean rhythm or freeze. Honest agents spend one credit per action; a fake carries k minting bills for k outputs.
